title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 13. Consoling Sarvabhauma
html:
The Lord resolves to visit the holy places and takes leave of Jagannatha, who bestows His garland on Him; He takes leave of Kashi Mishra and of Sarvabhauma and consoles them with the promise of a speedy return

Verse 1

एवं कतिपयं कालं क्रीडित्वा सह वैष्णवैः।
श्रीकाशीनाथमिश्रेण वैष्णवाग्र्येण धीमता॥१॥

evaṁ katipayaṁ kālaṁ krīḍitvā saha vaiṣṇavaiḥ|
śrīkāśīnāthamiśreṇa vaiṣṇavāgryeṇa dhīmatā||1||

evam — thus; katipayam — some; kalam — time; kriditva — having sported; saha — together; vaishnavaih — with the Vaishnavas; shri-kashinatha-mishrena — with Sri Kashinatha Mishra; vaishnava-agryena — the foremost of Vaishnavas; dhimata — wise.

1Thus for some time the Lord sported with the Vaishnavas. Then, having taken counsel with the wise Sri Kashinatha Mishra1, the foremost of Vaishnavas,

Verse 2

सम्मन्त्र्य भगवान्कृष्णस्तीर्थानां पावनेच्छया।
पुण्यान्यक्षेत्रगमने मतिं चक्रे महाद्युतिः॥२॥

sammantrya bhagavānkṛṣṇastīrthānāṁ pāvanecchayā|
puṇyānyakṣetragamane matiṁ cakre mahādyutiḥ||2||

sammantrya — having consulted; bhagavan — Bhagavan; krishnah — Krishna; tirthanam — of the holy places; pavana-ichchhaya — with the wish to purify; punya-anya-kshetra-gamane — on going to other holy lands; matim — resolve; chakre — made; maha-dyutih — of great splendour.

2Bhagavan Krishna, of great splendour, resolved to go to other holy lands in order to purify the tirthas.

Verse 3

ततो गत्वा जगन्नाथं दृष्ट्वा श्रीपुरुषोत्तमम्।
नत्वा तं भक्तिभावेन नेत्रधारापरिप्लुतः॥३॥

tato gatvā jagannāthaṁ dṛṣṭvā śrīpuruṣottamam|
natvā taṁ bhaktibhāvena netradhārāpariplutaḥ||3||

tatah — then; gatva — going; jagannatham — Jagannatha; drishtva — seeing; shri-purushottamam — Sri Purushottama; natva — bowing; tam — to Him; bhakti-bhavena — with devotion; netra-dhara-pariplutah — drenched with streams from His eyes.

3He went to Jagannatha and, beholding Sri Purushottama, bowed to Him with devotion, drenched with streams of tears from His eyes.

Verse 4

उवाच मधुरां वाणीं सगद्गदगिरा हरिः।
कृताञ्जलिपुटः प्रेमपरिपूर्णसुविग्रहः॥४॥

uvāca madhurāṁ vāṇīṁ sagadgadagirā hariḥ|
kṛtāñjalipuṭaḥ premaparipūrṇasuvigrahaḥ||4||

uvacha — spoke; madhuram — sweet; vanim — words; sa-gadgada-gira — in a faltering voice; harih — Hari; krita-anjali-putah — with joined palms; prema-paripurna-su-vigrahah — His beautiful form filled with love.

4With joined palms Hari, His beautiful form filled with love, addressed Him in a faltering voice with sweet words:

Verse 5

देव त्वत्क्षेत्रवासे मे नाधिकारो यतोऽभवत्।
ततोऽन्यक्षेत्रगमने मतिर्मे जायते प्रभो॥५॥

deva tvatkṣetravāse me nādhikāro yato'bhavat|
tato'nyakṣetragamane matirme jāyate prabho||5||

deva — O God; tvat-kshetra-vase — to dwell in Your land; me — of Me; na — no; adhikarah — right; yatah — since; abhavat — there proved to be; tatah — therefore; anya-kshetra-gamane — to go to other lands; matih — the wish; me — in Me; jayate — arises; prabho — O Lord.

5"O God, since I have no right to dwell in Your land, the wish has arisen in Me to go to other lands, O Lord.

Verse 6

वक्त्रं राकापतिप्रख्यं शरत्पङ्कजलोचनम्।
दीर्घबिम्बौष्ठरदनच्छदं साधु सुवक्षसम्॥६॥

vaktraṁ rākāpatiprakhyaṁ śaratpaṅkajalocanam|
dīrghabimbauṣṭharadanacchadaṁ sādhu suvakṣasam||6||

vaktram — the face; raka-pati-prakhyam — like the full moon; sharat-pankaja-lochanam — with eyes like autumn lotuses; dirgha-bimba-oshtha-radanachchhadam — with lips like long bimba fruits; sadhu — beautifully; su-vakshasam — broad-chested.

6Your face is like the full moon, Your eyes like autumn lotuses, Your lips like long bimba fruits, Your chest broad and beautiful:

Verse 7

दृष्ट्वा कस्य मनो याति क्षेत्रान्तरगतौ हरे।
तस्मान्नास्त्यत्र मे देव स्थितौ ते तादृशी कृपा॥७॥

dṛṣṭvā kasya mano yāti kṣetrāntaragatau hare|
tasmānnāstyatra me deva sthitau te tādṛśī kṛpā||7||

drishtva — having seen; kasya — whose; manah — mind; yati — would turn; kshetra-antara-gatau — to going to another land; hare — O Hari; tasmat — therefore; na asti — there is not; atra — here; me — for Me; deva — O God; sthitau — for staying; te — Your; tadrishi — such; kripa — mercy.

7who, having seen You, would wish to go to another land, O Hari? It must be that You have no such mercy for Me as would let Me stay here2.

Verse 8

क्षेत्राण्यन्यानि गच्छामि तव द्रष्टुं जनार्दन।
तथा मां कुरु मे देव यथा तीर्थमहं व्रजे॥८॥

kṣetrāṇyanyāni gacchāmi tava draṣṭuṁ janārdana|
tathā māṁ kuru me deva yathā tīrthamahaṁ vraje||8||

kshetrani — lands; anyani — other; gachchhami — I go; tava — Your; drashtum — to see; janardana — O Janardana; tatha — so; mam — Me; kuru — make; me — for Me; deva — O God; yatha — that; tirtham — to the tirthas; aham — I; vraje — may go.

8I shall go to see Your other lands, O Janardana. Grant, O God, that I may make My way to the tirthas.

Verse 9

यावत्स्याच्चञ्चलं चित्तं न स्याद्यावत्सुनिर्मलम्।
तावत्तीर्थानि पुण्यानि विचरेत्सर्वतः पुमान्॥९॥

yāvatsyāccañcalaṁ cittaṁ na syādyāvatsunirmalam|
tāvattīrthāni puṇyāni vicaretsarvataḥ pumān||9||

yavat — as long as; syat — is; chanchalam — restless; chittam — the mind; na — not; syat — is; yavat — as long as; su-nirmalam — perfectly pure; tavat — so long; tirthani — tirthas; punyani — holy; vicharet — should wander; sarvatah — everywhere; puman — a man.

9As long as the mind is restless and not yet perfectly pure, a man should wander everywhere among the holy tirthas.

Verse 10

ततः सुनिर्मले चित्ते स्थिरधीः पुरुषोत्तमे।
निवासं कुरुते नित्यं पथिकः स्वाश्रये यथा॥१०॥

tataḥ sunirmale citte sthiradhīḥ puruṣottame|
nivāsaṁ kurute nityaṁ pathikaḥ svāśraye yathā||10||

tatah — then; su-nirmale — perfectly pure; chitte — when the mind; sthira-dhih — steady of mind; purushottame — in Purushottama; nivasam — dwelling; kurute — makes; nityam — constant; pathikah — a traveller; sva-ashraye — in his own home; yatha — as.

10But when the mind has become perfectly pure, the man of steady mind settles for ever in Purushottama, as a traveller settles in his own home."

Verse 11

एवं वदति चैतन्ये ग्रीवायाश्चानुलम्बितम्।
माल्यं पपात कृष्णस्य पादसिंहासनोपरि॥११॥

evaṁ vadati caitanye grīvāyāścānulambitam|
mālyaṁ papāta kṛṣṇasya pādasiṁhāsanopari||11||

evam — thus; vadati — as was speaking; chaitanye — Chaitanya; grivayah — from the neck; cha — and; anulambitam — hanging; malyam — the garland; papata — fell; krishnasya — of Krishna; pada-simhasana-upari — onto the foot of the throne.

11As Chaitanya was speaking thus, the garland hanging from Krishna's neck fell onto the foot of His throne.

Verse 12

प्रतिहारी तदादाय जगन्नाथाज्ञया मुदा।
ददौ प्रसादरूपं तन्माल्यं चैतन्यमूर्धनि॥१२॥

pratihārī tadādāya jagannāthājñayā mudā|
dadau prasādarūpaṁ tanmālyaṁ caitanyamūrdhani||12||

pratihari — the door-keeper (temple servant); tat — it; adaya — taking; jagannatha-ajnaya — by Jagannatha's command; muda — joyfully; dadau — placed; prasada-rupam — as prasada (a token of grace); tat — that; malyam — garland; chaitanya-murdhani — on Chaitanya's head.

12By Jagannatha's command the temple door-keeper joyfully took it up and placed that garland on Chaitanya's head as a token of grace.

Verse 13

ततः सोऽपि महातेजाः प्रफुल्लवदनो हरिः।
स्वप्रेमनामसम्पूर्णो गच्छद्द्विरदविक्रमः॥१३॥

tataḥ so'pi mahātejāḥ praphullavadano hariḥ|
svapremanāmasampūrṇo gacchaddviradavikramaḥ||13||

tatah — then; sah — He; api — too; maha-tejah — of great splendour; praphulla-vadanah — His face blossoming; harih — Hari; sva-prema-nama-sampurnah — full of His love and of the names; gachchhat-dvirada-vikramah — with the gait of a striding elephant.

13Then Hari too, of great splendour, His face blossoming, full of love and of the holy names, set out with the gait of a striding elephant;

Verse 14

एवं लोकानुशिक्षार्थं भूत्वा प्रेमार्द्रलोचनः।
काशीमिश्राश्रमं गत्वा तं प्राह श्रीशचीसुतः॥१४॥

evaṁ lokānuśikṣārthaṁ bhūtvā premārdralocanaḥ|
kāśīmiśrāśramaṁ gatvā taṁ prāha śrīśacīsutaḥ||14||

evam — thus; loka-anushiksha-artham — to teach the people; bhutva — becoming; prema-ardra-lochanah — His eyes moist with love; kashi-mishra-ashramam — to the dwelling of Kashi Mishra; gatva — going; tam — to him; praha — said; shri-shachi-sutah — the son of Sri Shachi.

14and, to teach the people, the son of Sri Shachi, His eyes moist with love, came to the dwelling of Kashi Mishra and said to him:

Verse 15

भवन्त एव पश्यन्तु पुरुषोत्तममीश्वरम्।
अहं तीर्थाटने यामि जगन्नाथेन वञ्चितः॥१५॥

bhavanta eva paśyantu puruṣottamamīśvaram|
ahaṁ tīrthāṭane yāmi jagannāthena vañcitaḥ||15||

bhavantah — you; eva — yourselves; pashyantu — may see (behold); purushottamam — Purushottama; ishvaram — the Lord; aham — I; tirtha-atane — on pilgrimage to the tirthas; yami — go; jagannathena — by Jagannatha; vanchitah — deprived.

15"You may behold the Lord Purushottama, but I, deprived by Jagannatha, am going on pilgrimage to the tirthas."

Verse 16

तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथितो भूत्वा काशीनाथः प्रभोः पदे।
पपात दण्डवत्तस्मिन्क्षितौ स प्ररुरोद च॥१६॥

tacchrutvā vyathito bhūtvā kāśīnāthaḥ prabhoḥ pade|
papāta daṇḍavattasminkṣitau sa praruroda ca||16||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; vyathitah — distressed; bhutva — becoming; kashinathah — Kashinatha; prabhoh — of the Lord; pade — at the feet; papata — fell; danda-vat — like a staff; tasmin — on that; kshitau — ground; sah — he; praruroda — burst into tears; cha — and.

16Hearing this, Kashinatha was stricken with despair: he fell like a staff on the ground at the Lord's feet and burst into tears.

Verse 17

कथं नाभूत्पुत्रशोको महारुग्णोऽभवन्न किम्।
चैतन्यचरणाम्भोजविश्लेषोऽयं कथं मम॥१७॥

kathaṁ nābhūtputraśoko mahārugṇo'bhavanna kim|
caitanyacaraṇāmbhojaviśleṣo'yaṁ kathaṁ mama||17||

katham — why; na — not; abhut — was there; putra-shokah — grief for a son; maha-rugnah — gravely ill; abhavam — I became; na kim — why not; chaitanya-charana-ambhoja-vishleshah — separation from Chaitanya's lotus feet; ayam — this; katham — why; mama — mine.

17"Why did the grief of losing a son not befall me? Why did I not fall gravely ill? Why instead has this separation from Chaitanya's lotus feet come to me?"

Verse 18

एवं स विलुठन्भूमौ शोकपूर्णो मुहुर्मुहुः।
सान्त्वितः करुणार्द्रेण पुनरागमनादिना॥१८॥

evaṁ sa viluṭhanbhūmau śokapūrṇo muhurmuhuḥ|
sāntvitaḥ karuṇārdreṇa punarāgamanādinā||18||

evam — thus; sah — he; viluthan — rolling; bhumau — on the ground; shoka-purnah — full of grief; muhuh muhuh — again and again; santvitah — was consoled; karuna-ardrena — by Him whose heart melted with compassion; punah-agamana-adina — with the promise of returning and other words.

18Thus, full of grief, he rolled on the ground again and again, and the Lord, His heart melting with compassion, consoled him with the promise of returning and with other words.

Verse 19

ततः श्रीसार्वभौमस्य गृहं गत्वा जगद्गुरुः।
आज्ञां ययाचे भगवांस्तीर्थानां गमनेच्छया॥१९॥

tataḥ śrīsārvabhaumasya gṛhaṁ gatvā jagadguruḥ|
ājñāṁ yayāce bhagavāṁstīrthānāṁ gamanecchayā||19||

tatah — then; shri-sarvabhaumasya — of Sri Sarvabhauma; griham — to the house; gatva — going; jagat-guruh — the Teacher of the world; ajnam — leave; yayache — asked; bhagavan — Bhagavan; tirthanam — to the tirthas; gamana-ichchhaya — wishing to go.

19Then Bhagavan, the Teacher of the world, went to the house of Sri Sarvabhauma and asked his leave to set out for the tirthas.

Verse 20

श्रुत्वा सरोदनं प्राह धृत्वा कृष्णपदाम्बुजम्।
कथं नाभूद्वज्रपातः शिरसि मे महाभुज॥२०॥

śrutvā sarodanaṁ prāha dhṛtvā kṛṣṇapadāmbujam|
kathaṁ nābhūdvajrapātaḥ śirasi me mahābhuja||20||

shrutva — hearing; sa-rodanam — with sobs; praha — said; dhritva — clasping; krishna-pada-ambujam — Krishna's lotus feet; katham — why; na — not; abhut — was there; vajra-patah — the stroke of a thunderbolt; shirasi — on the head; me — my; maha-bhuja — O mighty-armed one.

20Hearing this, Sarvabhauma clasped Krishna's lotus feet and said with sobs, "Why has a thunderbolt not struck my head, O mighty-armed one?

Verse 21

त्वत्पादरहितं प्राणं कथं धास्याम्यहं प्रभो।
मां गृहीत्वा यत्र कुत्र गमनं कर्तुमर्हसि॥२१॥

tvatpādarahitaṁ prāṇaṁ kathaṁ dhāsyāmyahaṁ prabho|
māṁ gṛhītvā yatra kutra gamanaṁ kartumarhasi||21||

tvat-pada-rahitam — bereft of Your feet; pranam — life; katham — how; dhasyami — shall sustain; aham — I; prabho — O Lord; mam — me; grihitva — taking; yatra kutra — wherever; gamanam — the journey; kartum — to make; arhasi — You should.

21How shall I keep my life without Your feet, O Lord? Take me with You wherever You go!"

Verse 22

एवं श्रुत्वा प्रहस्यासौ धृत्वा तस्य करद्वयम्।
आगमिष्याम्यदीर्घेण कालेनेत्याह केशवः॥२२॥

evaṁ śrutvā prahasyāsau dhṛtvā tasya karadvayam|
āgamiṣyāmyadīrgheṇa kālenetyāha keśavaḥ||22||

evam — thus; shrutva — hearing; prahasya — laughing; asau — He; dhritva — taking; tasya — his; kara-dvayam — two hands; agamishyami — I shall return; adirghena — not long; kalena — in time (soon); iti — thus; aha — said; keshavah — Keshava.

22Hearing this, Keshava laughed, took him by both hands and said, "I shall return before long."

Verse 23

वदन्तं तं समालिङ्ग्य करुणापूर्णविग्रहः।
सान्त्वयामास स्वप्रेम्णा नानानुनयकोविदः॥२३॥

vadantaṁ taṁ samāliṅgya karuṇāpūrṇavigrahaḥ|
sāntvayāmāsa svapremṇā nānānunayakovidaḥ||23||

vadantam — speaking; tam — him; samalingya — embracing; karuna-purna-vigrahah — whose form is full of compassion; santvayam asa — consoled; sva-premna — with His love; nana-anunaya-kovidah — skilled in many ways of comforting.

23And, embracing him while he was still speaking, the Lord, whose form is full of compassion and who is skilled in every way of comforting, consoled him with His love.

Thus ends the thirteenth sarga, "Consoling Sarvabhauma" (Sarvabhauma-santvana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Kashinatha Mishra (Kashi Mishra): a Vaishnava of Puri, in whose house the Lord later lived.
  2. The Lord speaks in loving self-abasement: He explains His wish to leave such beauty by saying that Jagannatha has not granted Him the mercy to stay.
